column1: # One claim per (subject, feature) pair. The other ledgers state a serving
# tuple, a pairing, a search grant, or an image grant; each of those implies
# something about what a reader can do with a checkpoint, and a reader
# assembling that implication row by row reconstructs it differently every
# time. This ledger states the implication once, so remote/build-feature-roster.sh
# emits webui/roster.json from a claim rather than from an inference over four
# subject_id names a row of the ledger the feature belongs to, and the feature
# decides which ledger that is. text-chat, vision, tool-selection,
# guarded-tool-execution, long-context, context-checkpoints, and quarantine name
# a remote/models.tsv id; draft-pair-speculation names a remote/draft-pairs.tsv
# pair_id; web-search names a remote/web-profiles.tsv profile_id;
# image-generation and image-review name a remote/image-profiles.tsv
# profile_id. One namespace per feature keeps the subject column free of a
# scope field that a typo would put at odds with the id beside it.
# status is closed over five values, and each states what a run has established.
# production is a claim measured safe and useful, the vocabulary
# remote/models.tsv gives its own tier field. candidate leaves quality or
# performance unqualified while a run has established the mechanism works.
# experimental names a mechanism the tree carries with the measurement still
# ahead of it, and its note names the run that moves it. unstable names a
# reset, fault, device loss, or correctness hazard, and its evidence is the
# record of that failure. unsupported names a mechanism this row reaches
# through a path nothing in the tree arms.
# evidence is a repository-relative path under evidence/ or `-`. production,
# candidate, and unstable require a path, because those three assert a run;
# experimental and unsupported admit `-`, because a mechanism nobody measured
# retains nothing. remote/check-ledger-evidence.sh asserts that every path a
# row names exists where the tree is, which is a property of the tree rather
# than of the row, so the generator validates row shape alone and the appliance
# reads this file over a directory the sync never sent.
# note carries the mechanism in one clause and stays free of the quotation mark
# and the backslash, because the generator writes it into a JSON string field
# and a ledger that cannot express an escape cannot emit invalid JSON.
# A (subject, feature) pair absent from this file emits status unclaimed, so
# the matrix reads a hole as the absence of a claim rather than as a denial.
